## This is exactly how we reproduce the mistake that exposes your data.

### We look for your tables

We try the table names most common in real apps — the same starting point anyone with your public URL would have.

## Why this matters right now

2026 security research found hundreds of apps built with these tools exposing full user records because of a single security policy left off. The pattern keeps repeating because AI tools generate the connection to the database, but don't always turn on the permission layer.

- We don't store your anon key after the scan finishes

- We never write, modify, or delete anything in your project

- We only check what's already publicly reachable from a browser

- The same classifier used here runs in production inside TrustBoost

## Acceptable Use Rules

This scanner performs read-only checks against publicly reachable Supabase endpoints, using the anonymous key already exposed in your app's client-side code.

### You must confirm authorization

You may only scan a project you own, or one you have explicit permission to test. Scanning a third party's project without authorization is not permitted, and access attempts are logged.

### What the scanner will never do

- Attempt to bypass authentication or exploit a vulnerability beyond confirming that data is exposed

- Write, modify, or delete any data

- Retrieve more than a small read-only sample from each table

### Fix requests

If you purchase a fix, we will never ask for your service_role key as a first step. You'll receive the exact SQL to run yourself in your own Supabase SQL editor, with guidance, and we re-verify the result using the same read-only scan. Hands-on access, if ever needed, is granted temporarily and only with your explicit approval.

### No guarantee

Results are best-effort and based on common table names and default configurations. A clean scan does not guarantee your application has no security issues — it is not a substitute for a full professional security audit.

## Privacy Policy

### What we collect

- The project URL and anon key you submit — used only to run the scan, and never written to our database

- A hashed version of your IP address, kept temporarily to enforce fair-use rate limits

- If you purchase a report or fix: the contact email you provide

### Payments

Paid reports and fixes are processed by a third-party payment provider. We do not receive or store your card details.

### Aggregate statistics

We may keep anonymized, aggregate figures (for example, "X% of scanned tables lacked a security policy") for research and public write-ups. These never identify your project or organization.

### Your rights

You can request deletion of any contact information we hold about you at any time by reaching out through the contact details provided at checkout.
